notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0004] Money-moving functions take idempotency_key and check it first: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept a keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Check it before any validation or state change: scan `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an entry with the same key and return the original result (the same record) without reapplying; pass `idempotency_key` into `audit.record`.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Validation failures in ledgerly raise BillingError(code, detail) with snake_case codes such as "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount"; follow this pattern instead of ValueError or bare exceptions.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0005] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and `approved_by` is missing; amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

candidate.content: State transitions in ledgerly/payments.py and ledgerly/invoice.py must raise BillingError("invalid_state", f"<entity> {id} is {status}") when the current status is wrong, before mutating anything.

item.title: Normalize timestamps with ensure_utc before storing
item.content: Always wrap incoming datetimes with ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc before storing them on models (e.g. payment.captured_at) or passing to audit.record.
